title: Circuit failover, temporal throttling, and tenant-led escalation logbook
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Summary: Production incidents observed Feb 11-12 where tenant bursts caused a short-lived 5xx amplification and elevated timeouts across the Hosted API. Symptoms: large sustained burst from a single tenant produced KV cache churn, proxy queue growth, increased RPC latency to the runtime, and client retries that amplified load. Impact: multiple customers experienced partial failures and elevated latencies (p50->p95 delta > 3x for 30-90s windows). Dedicated/private deployments saw similar user patterns but did not surface the same proxy-level queueing because of reserved capacity; however, on-prem edge misconfigs replicated parts of the failure chain.

Root cause (summary):
- A tenant burst evicted hot prefixes from the KV cache (inefficient prefix eviction heuristics for long sequences) which increased token-generation latency for subsequent streaming requests.
- Edge proxy admission did not apply tenant-scoped short-term throttles; requests queued at the front door increasing connection hold times.
- SDK and customer integrations performed aggressive immediate retries (default 3 rapid retries) without jitter, leading to retry amplification when backpressure started.
- The combination triggered a cascading timeout wave where some runtime workers returned 5xx for inflight requests under memory pressure.

Immediate mitigations enacted (Feb 12-14):
- Deployed edge hotpatch to introduce a per-tenant short-window token-bucket (temporal throttling) that caps burst rate for 60s windows and allows fast recovery after the window.
- Enabled failure-sensitive circuit-breaker mode at proxy (trips earlier for high-latency signals) and routes affected tenants to a lightweight fallback pool (smaller-model variant) to preserve SLOs.
- Rolled out SDK guidance and a one-line server-side shim to add jittered exponential backoff for retries and to recommend idempotency tokens for high-throughput clients.
- Emergency KV-cache heuristic tweak: reduce eviction aggressiveness for in-flight prefixes and enabled a short-lived sticky cache for top N prefixes per-tenant.

Permanent plan and work items:
- Replace current prefix eviction heuristics with LRU+frequency-aware policy tuned for streaming workloads (runtime change, estimate: 5 points).
- Implement a server-side replay-safe retry-dedup layer to collapse duplicate retries within a short window (2s) per idempotency token.
- Add a tenant-priority fastpath that can transparently degrade models or offload to dedicated burst-capacity when tenant exceeds negotiated burst profiles.
- Expand monitoring: per-tenant queue depth, per-proxy connection hold time, retry amplification metric, and a derived tenant-instability score with alert thresholds.
- Create a standardized customer-escalation logbook (this ticket) and embed an automated feedback tick that records customer comms, assigned SE, and follow-ups.

Rollout and verification:
- Hotpatch validated in the canary region (us-west-1) Feb 13 with synthetic tenant bursts; observed queue depth falls by ~70% and 5xx spikes eliminated in test windows.
- Staged rollout to global edge completed Feb 14 02:00 UTC. Production telemetry shows incident windows shortened from ~90s to <15s in subsequent bursts.
- Verification plan: 48h stabilization window followed by a config-controlled rollout of the permanent KV cache change in runtime-1.20. Post-deploy KPI: p95 latency regression <= 3% and retry-amplification metric below 0.05.

Customer communications & runbook:
- Created focused customer comms templates for P1 escalations and provided recommended SDK changes to affected customers.
- Runbook updated: "tenant-burst -> apply temporal-throttle -> route to fallback -> notify SE & CS" with playbook links below.

Scope notes:
- Hosted: full mitigation and rollout managed by platform.
- Dedicated: recommend customer apply temporal-throttle policy via admin console; provide guidance and patch for shared autoscaling policies.
- Private/on-prem: deliver configuration recipe and small runtime patch; customer must coordinate upgrade for sticky cache and eviction heuristics.

Success criteria:
- No customer-visible 5xx amplification incidents for the same root cause pattern in 30 days post-full rollout.
- Automated alerts trigger before p95 latency crosses threshold, allowing proactive rate-limiting.
- Customers adopt recommended SDK backoff within 2 weeks for those who reached out.
